definitionEn: To use money to buy things or pay for services.
example: I try not to spend too much money on clothes each month.

definitionEn: The amount of money needed to buy something.
example: The price of petrol has risen sharply over the past year.

definitionEn: Money in the form of coins or notes, not cards or cheques.
example: Many small shops still prefer to be paid in cash.

definitionEn: The fixed amount of money someone receives each month for their job.
example: She accepted the job mainly because of the generous salary.

definitionEn: To receive money in return for work or services.
example: He earns a good living by teaching English online.

definitionEn: A piece of paper showing that you have paid for something.
example: Always keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.

definitionEn: Something bought for much less than its usual price.
example: We found a real bargain at the sale on Saturday morning.

definitionEn: A reduction in the usual price of something.
example: Students get a ten percent discount on all train tickets.

definitionEn: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.
example: Living in the city centre is far more expensive than in the suburbs.

definitionEn: To have enough money to pay for something.
example: Many young families cannot afford to buy a house nowadays.

definitionEn: To keep money over time in order to buy something later.
example: They saved up enough money for a holiday in Japan next summer.

definitionEn: To take money or things from someone and give them back later.
example: I had to borrow money from my parents to pay the rent.

definitionEn: To have to pay someone money that you received from them earlier.
example: He still owes his brother two hundred dollars from last year.

definitionEn: Money returned to a customer after a purchase is cancelled or returned.
example: The shop gave me a full refund because the jacket was faulty.

definitionEn: Money paid to a worker, usually weekly or hourly, for their work.
example: Many factory workers receive a minimum wage for their long hours.

definitionEn: The system of money used in a particular country.
example: The euro is the official currency in many European countries.

definitionEn: An extra sum of money given to an employee as a reward.
example: Staff received a generous year-end bonus after the company's best season.

definitionEn: A fee paid to someone for selling goods or arranging a deal.
example: The estate agent earns a commission of two percent on each sale.

definitionEn: Extra money paid on savings, or charged on money borrowed.
example: The bank pays a low rate of interest on children's savings accounts.

definitionEn: An amount of money or goods left over after needs are met.
example: The government used its budget surplus to repay part of the national debt.

definitionEn: The amount by which spending is greater than income.
example: The company reported a deficit of several million pounds last quarter.

definitionEn: A document listing goods or services supplied and the amount due.
example: Please send the invoice to our accounts department by Friday.

definitionEn: A written statement of the amount of money owed for goods or services.
example: We received the electricity bill, and it was much higher than usual.

definitionEn: A sum of money charged for a service or for permission to do something.
example: The bank charges a monthly fee if the balance falls below a limit.

definitionEn: A cost of doing something that a person or business must pay.
example: Travel expenses are reimbursed only when you attach the original receipts.

definitionEn: A situation where the amount of something is less than what is needed.
example: The charity faced a shortfall in donations after the economic downturn.

definitionEn: Not too expensive for most people to pay for.
example: Affordable housing is a major concern for young couples in big cities.

definitionEn: Having enough money to pay all debts that are due.
example: The firm remained solvent despite losing its largest client last year.

definitionEn: A debt or financial obligation that a person or company must pay.
example: The company's total liabilities now exceed the value of its assets.

definitionEn: Something valuable owned by a person or company, such as property.
example: Her house is her most valuable asset, worth far more than her savings.

definitionEn: The value of an owner's share in a property or company after debts.
example: He built up home equity by paying down his mortgage for twenty years.

definitionEn: A regular amount paid to an insurance company for cover.
example: Her insurance premium rose sharply after she made a claim.

definitionEn: Protection against financial loss, paid for through regular payments.
example: Everyone who drives a car must have valid insurance under the law.

definitionEn: To leave something valuable with a lender as security for a loan.
example: He had to pawn his watch to pay urgent bills last month.

definitionEn: Shares of ownership in a company that can be bought and sold.
example: She bought stock in a renewable energy company last spring.

definitionEn: A very large amount of money or wealth owned by a person.
example: He made a fortune selling software before he turned thirty.

definitionEn: A document showing how much pay a worker receives and what was deducted.
example: Check your payslip carefully to make sure the tax is correct.

definitionEn: A written order to a bank to pay money from your account to someone.
example: Could you make the cheque payable to the company, please?

definitionEn: An act of buying, selling, or transferring money between two parties.
example: Every online transaction is protected by a secure encryption system.

definitionEn: The act of paying back money that was borrowed, usually in parts.
example: Monthly repayments on the car loan will finish in March next year.

definitionEn: To spend more money than you have or than you planned.
example: Many families overspend during the holidays and struggle in January.

definitionEn: To experience financial difficulty because money is scarce.
example: Many workers began to feel the pinch after prices rose so quickly.

definitionEn: To earn exactly as much money as you spend, so there is no profit.
example: The new café should break even within its first year of trading.

definitionEn: To earn just enough money to pay for basic living costs.
example: Working two jobs was the only way she could make ends meet.

definitionEn: Having a negative bank balance or losing money in business.
example: The company has been in the red for three consecutive years now.

definitionEn: The amount of money needed to pay for everyday expenses like food and rent.
example: The rising cost of living has hit low-income families the hardest.

meaningVi: thuộc tài khoá, tài chính công
definitionEn: Relating to government revenue, spending, and public debt.
example: The government announced a fiscal policy aimed at reducing the deficit.

definitionEn: Relating to money or to the currency system of a country.
example: The central bank raised interest rates as part of its monetary policy.

definitionEn: To decrease in value over time, especially a vehicle or equipment.
example: Most new cars depreciate sharply during their first three years.

definitionEn: To increase in value over a period of time.
example: Property in this district has appreciated considerably over the last decade.

definitionEn: A sustained fall in general price levels across an economy.
example: Economists warned that prolonged deflation could slow economic growth sharply.

definitionEn: Government spending or action designed to boost economic activity.
example: The government unveiled a massive stimulus package to support struggling businesses.

definitionEn: Strict government measures to reduce spending during an economic crisis.
example: Years of austerity left many public services underfunded and overstretched.

definitionEn: Money that is owed and remains unpaid after the due date.
example: The tenant fell into arrears after losing his job in the spring.

definitionEn: To sell off a company's assets in order to pay its debts.
example: The directors decided to liquidate the company after months of losses.

definitionEn: The use of borrowed money to increase the potential return of an investment.
example: Investors often use leverage to magnify gains, but losses can grow just as fast.

definitionEn: Buying something in hope of profit from future price changes.
example: Wild speculation in the housing market eventually pushed prices beyond reach.

definitionEn: The tendency of prices or markets to change rapidly and unpredictably.
example: Market volatility increased sharply after the unexpected election result.

definitionEn: To make a harmful or unpleasant situation less severe.
example: Companies must mitigate financial risks by diversifying their investments carefully.

definitionEn: The ability of a plan or business to succeed and be sustainable.
example: The consultants questioned the long-term viability of the proposed project.

definitionEn: An additional fee charged on top of the normal price of something.
example: Airlines often add a fuel surcharge to the price of every ticket.

definitionEn: A tax or fee imposed by a government or authority.
example: The council plans to introduce a new levy on tourist accommodation.

definitionEn: Money or payment given to someone in return for work or services.
example: Executives' remuneration packages have attracted criticism from many shareholders.

definitionEn: To guarantee financial support for a project and accept its risks.
example: The bank agreed to underwrite the entire cost of the new bridge.

definitionEn: To pay off a debt through regular payments over a fixed period.
example: The loan is designed to amortise over twenty-five years of monthly payments.

definitionEn: The ability of a person or business to meet long-term financial obligations.
example: Analysts are concerned about the solvency of several regional banks.

definitionEn: To collect and store large amounts of something, often secretly.
example: During the crisis, many people began to hoard cash at home.

definitionEn: Acting carefully and wisely, especially in managing money or risks.
example: It is prudent to keep an emergency fund equal to six months' expenses.

definitionEn: Much higher than is reasonable or acceptable in cost.
example: The hotel charged exorbitant prices for drinks and room service.

definitionEn: Producing a large amount of profit or money.
example: She left teaching for a more lucrative career in corporate finance.

definitionEn: Showing off wealth in a way intended to attract attention and admiration.
example: The ostentatious display of jewellery at the party embarrassed many guests.

definitionEn: To cheat someone by charging them far too much money.
example: Unscrupulous traders fleeced tourists who were unfamiliar with local prices.

definitionEn: Likely to cause a general rise in prices across an economy.
example: Economists warned that the new spending plan could be inflationary.

definitionEn: A collection of investments owned by a person or institution.
example: A diversified portfolio helps reduce the risk of major losses.

definitionEn: A continual change up and down in amount, level, or price.
example: Currency fluctuations make it difficult to plan long-term export contracts.

definitionEn: The state of owing money, or the total amount that is owed.
example: Household indebtedness has risen steadily since interest rates began falling.

definitionEn: Relating to a legal duty to act in another person's financial interest.
example: Financial advisers have a fiduciary duty to act in their clients' best interests.

definitionEn: The ease with which an asset can be turned into cash without losing value.
example: The firm needs more liquidity to cover its short-term debts this quarter.

definitionEn: Financial rescue given to a failing business or bank by an outside party.
example: The government refused to provide a bailout for the struggling airline.

definitionEn: Relating to money, especially in the context of financial gain or loss.
example: The committee dismissed the claim, citing a lack of pecuniary motive.

definitionEn: Motivated only by the desire for money or personal gain.
example: Critics accused the consultant of having purely mercenary motives for the merger.

definitionEn: Unwilling to spend money or use resources; extremely careful with money.
example: His parsimonious habits meant he rarely bought anything for himself.

definitionEn: Extremely poor, lacking the money needed for basic necessities.
example: The penurious author wrote his finest novel in a freezing attic.

definitionEn: Having little or no money; habitually short of funds.
example: Many impecunious students rely on part-time work to pay their tuition.

definitionEn: Spending money or resources recklessly and wastefully.
example: The profligate heir squandered the family fortune within a decade.

definitionEn: Expensive, rich, and lavish, especially in food, furnishings or dress.
example: The guests were served a sumptuous banquet of seafood and rare wines.

definitionEn: Great wealth or luxury, especially as shown in surroundings or lifestyle.
example: The palace was furnished with a staggering opulence that impressed every visitor.

definitionEn: Great generosity in giving money or gifts to others.
example: The philanthropist's munificence funded three new hospitals across the region.

definitionEn: An extreme and greedy desire for wealth and possessions.
example: Dickens portrayed avarice as a corrupting force in Victorian society.

definitionEn: An eager desire to acquire wealth, often in an improper way.
example: The scandal exposed the cupidity of several senior board members.

definitionEn: A very small amount of money, especially as payment for work.
example: Workers were paid a pittance for backbreaking labour in the mines.

definitionEn: A fixed regular sum of money paid to someone such as a student or clergy member.
example: Doctoral students receive a modest monthly stipend while conducting their research.

definitionEn: Money or benefits received from employment or an office.
example: The post carries generous emoluments, including housing and a private car.

definitionEn: Trickery or deception used to gain a financial or legal advantage.
example: The company's accounts were full of chicanery designed to hide its losses.

definitionEn: The practice of lending money at extremely high interest rates.
example: Laws against usury were introduced to protect poor borrowers from exploitation.

definitionEn: Money or property left to someone in a will.
example: She received a generous bequest from an aunt she barely knew.

definitionEn: Generous giving of money or gifts, often to inferiors or the public.
example: The wealthy patron distributed largesse to the artists and musicians of the city.

definitionEn: A paid job requiring little or no work, often given as a favour.
example: The minister's brother held a lucrative sinecure with the state railways.

definitionEn: Dangerously uncertain or in a very bad state, especially financially.
example: The company's parlous finances forced it to cut hundreds of jobs.

definitionEn: Poor to the point of lacking the basic necessities of life.
example: Charities provide free meals for indigent families during the winter months.

definitionEn: A person who is extremely careful and stingy about spending money.
example: My grandmother was a pinchpenny who reused every paper bag she received.

definitionEn: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.
example: The moneyed elite of the city had lived in the district for generations.

definitionEn: A sum of money demanded in return for releasing a captured person.
example: The kidnappers demanded a ransom of two million dollars for the hostage's release.

definitionEn: The national treasury or the funds controlled by a government.
example: Rising welfare costs have placed a heavy strain on the public exchequer.

definitionEn: The act of paying out money from a fund or account.
example: The foundation's disbursement of grants was delayed by administrative errors.

definitionEn: The crime of obtaining money from someone by threats or force.
example: Police arrested two men accused of extortion against local shop owners.

definitionEn: To steal money that has been entrusted to you by an employer.
example: The accountant was jailed after he embezzled funds from the charity.

definitionEn: To waste money or an opportunity carelessly and foolishly.
example: He squandered his inheritance on expensive cars and failed investments.

definitionEn: The money or resources needed to do something.
example: Few small firms have the wherewithal to fund such an expensive research programme.

definitionEn: Wealth regarded as a corrupting influence or an excessive pursuit.
example: The novel warns readers against worshipping mammon above all human values.

definitionEn: Spending money or resources in a wasteful, reckless way.
example: The prodigal son spent every penny of his father's wealth in a single year.

definitionEn: Very reluctant to spend money or to give generously to others.
example: The niggardly landlord refused to repair the broken heating system.

definitionEn: An informal term for someone who hates spending money.
example: Nobody wanted to split the bill with such a notorious tightwad.

definitionEn: To be very careful about spending small amounts of money.
example: Students often have to pinch pennies to survive until the next loan.

definitionEn: A person, often a monk, who lives by begging for alms.
example: The mendicant monks walked from village to village asking for food.

definitionEn: A severe shortage or lack of something that is needed.
example: There is a dearth of affordable credit for small rural businesses.

definitionEn: Extreme poverty, or the condition of having no money at all.
example: The writer lived in penury for years before his novels became famous.

definitionEn: A sum of money given in appreciation of service, such as a tip.
example: A service gratuity of fifteen percent is added to your bill automatically.

definitionEn: Payment or compensation given for loss, injury, or work done.
example: The family sought recompense for the damage caused by the faulty wiring.

definitionEn: Money, especially when it is regarded as a base or greedy goal.
example: Some critics accused the artist of chasing filthy lucre rather than meaning.
